title: Motion in a Straight Line and Plane — 40 MCQs
description: Comprehensive multiple-choice questions covering instantaneous velocity and acceleration, relative velocity, graphical equations of motion, freely falling bodies, and projectile motion.

questions.q: What does the slope of a displacement-time graph at any given point represent?
questions.explanation: The slope of the tangent at any point on a displacement-time graph gives the rate of change of displacement, which is instantaneous velocity.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity with respect to time, measured in meters per second squared (m/s²).

questions.q: What is the acceleration of a freely falling body near the surface of the Earth, neglecting air resistance?
questions.explanation: A freely falling body experiences a constant acceleration due to gravity, which is approximately 9.8 m/s² directed downwards.

questions.q: What does the area under a velocity-time graph represent?
questions.explanation: The area under a velocity-time graph integrated over time yields the total displacement of the object.

questions.q: At the highest point of a projectile's trajectory, its vertical component of velocity is:
questions.explanation: At the peak of its trajectory, the projectile momentarily stops moving vertically before falling back down, so its vertical velocity is zero.

questions.q: If two cars are moving in the same direction with equal velocities, what is their relative velocity?
questions.explanation: Relative velocity of object A with respect to B is vA - vB. When velocities are equal, the difference is zero.

questions.q: The path followed by a projectile is known as its:
questions.explanation: The curved path that an object follows under the action of gravity is called its trajectory.

questions.q: Which of the following physical quantities is vector in nature?
questions.explanation: Velocity has both magnitude and direction, making it a vector quantity, whereas speed, distance, and time are scalars.

questions.q: When a body is dropped freely from a tower, its initial velocity is:
questions.explanation: When a body is dropped from rest, its initial velocity is zero.

questions.q: The slope of a velocity-time graph represents:
questions.explanation: The rate of change of velocity with time is acceleration, which corresponds to the slope of a velocity-time graph.

questions.q: For a projectile launched from the ground, the horizontal component of acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Assuming air resistance is negligible, there are no horizontal forces acting on a projectile, so its horizontal acceleration is zero.

questions.q: An object moves along a straight line such that its position x = 3t. What is its velocity?
questions.explanation: Velocity is the derivative of position with respect to time: v = dx/dt = d(3t)/dt = 3 m/s.

questions.q: What is the angle of projection for maximum horizontal range on level ground?
questions.explanation: The range formula R = (u² sin(2θ))/g yields the maximum value when sin(2θ) = 1, which means 2θ = 90 degrees or θ = 45 degrees.

questions.q: If a car starts from rest and attains a velocity of 20 m/s in 5 s, its average acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Acceleration = (v - u) / t = (20 - 0) / 5 = 4 m/s².

questions.q: Which equation of motion is independent of time t?
questions.explanation: The third equation of motion, v² - u² = 2as, relates initial velocity, final velocity, acceleration, and displacement without involving time t.

questions.q: A particle moves along the x-axis with position given by x(t) = 4t² + 2t + 5. What is its instantaneous velocity at t = 2 s?
questions.explanation: Velocity v(t) = dx/dt = 8t + 2. At t = 2 s, v(2) = 8(2) + 2 = 18 m/s.

questions.q: Two trains are moving on parallel tracks in opposite directions with speeds 30 m/s and 20 m/s. What is the relative velocity of the first train with respect to the second?
questions.explanation: Taking the direction of the first train as positive, v1 = 30 m/s and v2 = -20 m/s. Relative velocity = v1 - v2 = 30 - (-20) = 50 m/s.

questions.q: A body is thrown vertically upwards with an initial velocity of 19.6 m/s. What is the total time taken to return to the point of projection? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Time to reach max height is t = u/g = 19.6 / 9.8 = 2 s. Total time of flight is twice the time to reach maximum height, so 2 * 2 = 4 s.

questions.q: A stone is dropped from the top of a cliff and hits the ground after 3 seconds. What is the height of the cliff? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
A projectile is fired with an initial velocity of 20 m/s at an angle of 30 degrees to the horizontal. What is the maximum height reached? (g = 10 m/s²)
An object accelerates from rest at a constant rate of 3 m/s² for 4 seconds, then moves with constant velocity for 5 seconds. What is the total distance covered?
questions.explanation: Distance in first phase s1 = 0.5 * 3 * (4)² = 24 m. Velocity at end of phase 1 is v = 3 * 4 = 12 m/s. Distance in second phase s2 = 12 * 5 = 60 m. Total distance = 24 + 60 = 84 m.

questions.q: A swimmer can swim in still water at 4 m/s. She crosses a river 40 m wide flowing at 3 m/s perpendicular to the current. What is her drift downstream?
questions.explanation: Time to cross t = width / velocity in water = 40 / 4 = 10 s. Drift = river speed * time = 3 m/s * 10 s = 30 m.

questions.q: The velocity of a particle moving along a straight line is given by v = 4t - t². What is its acceleration at t = 2 s?
questions.explanation: Acceleration a = dv/dt = d(4t - t²)/dt = 4 - 2t. At t = 2 s, a = 4 - 2(2) = 0 m/s².

questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upwards and reaches a height of 20 m. What was its initial velocity? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Using v² - u² = -2gh (at peak v = 0), 0 - u² = -2(10)(20) -> u² = 400 -> u = 20 m/s.

questions.q: A body covers 10 m in the 2nd second and 25 m in the 5th second of its motion with uniform acceleration. What is its initial velocity?
questions.explanation: Sn = u + a/2(2n-1). For n=2, 10 = u + 1.5a. For n=5, 25 = u + 4.5a. Solving these equations gives a = 5 m/s² and u = 2.5 m/s.

questions.q: A projectile has a range of 100 m. If it is launched at an angle of 30 degrees to the horizontal, what is its initial velocity? (g = 10 m/s²)
A car accelerates uniformly from 10 m/s to 30 m/s in 4 seconds. Using a velocity-time graph or formula, what is the distance traveled during this time?
questions.explanation: Distance = average velocity * time = ((10 + 30) / 2) * 4 = 20 * 4 = 80 m.

questions.q: Two bodies of different masses are dropped simultaneously from the same height in vacuum. Which statement is correct?
questions.explanation: In a vacuum, acceleration due to gravity is independent of mass, so all bodies fall with the same acceleration and hit the ground simultaneously.

questions.q: A projectile is thrown such that its horizontal range is equal to three times its maximum height. What is the angle of projection?
questions.explanation: R = 3H -> (u² sin(2θ))/g = 3 * (u² sin²(θ))/(2g) -> 2 sin(θ)cos(θ) = 3/2 sin²(θ) -> tan(θ) = 4/3 -> θ = atan(4/3).

questions.q: An elevator is moving upwards with an acceleration of 2 m/s². A person inside drops a coin from a height of 2 m. What is the effective acceleration of the coin relative to the elevator? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Effective acceleration a_eff = g + a_elevator = 9.8 + 2 = 11.8 m/s² downwards relative to the elevator.

questions.q: The position vector of a particle is given by r = (3t³ i + 4t² j) m. What is the magnitude of its acceleration at t = 1 s?
questions.explanation: Velocity v = dr/dt = 9t² i + 8t j. Acceleration a = dv/dt = 18t i + 8 j. At t = 1 s, magnitude = root(18² + 8²) = root(388) approx 19.7 m/s².

questions.q: A particle moves in the xy-plane with velocity components vx = 6t and vy = 2. If it starts from the origin at t = 0, what is the equation of its trajectory (y in terms of x)?
questions.explanation: x = integral(6t dt) = 3t² -> t = root(x/3). y = integral(2 dt) = 2t = 2 root(x/3).

questions.q: A ball is projected from the top of a tower 40 m high with a horizontal velocity of 10 m/s. How far from the base of the tower does the ball hit the ground? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Time to fall h = 0.5 gt² -> 40 = 0.5 * 10 * t² -> t = root(8) = 2.828 s. Horizontal distance = u * t = 10 * 2.828 = 28.3 m.

questions.q: An airplane is flying horizontally with a speed of 360 km/h at an altitude of 2000 m. At what horizontal distance before the target should a bomb be released to hit it? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Speed = 360 km/h = 100 m/s. Time to fall t = root(2h/g) = root(4000/10) = 20 s. Horizontal distance = 100 m/s * 20 s = 2000 m.

questions.q: Rain is falling vertically with a speed of 10 m/s. A person is running eastwards with a speed of 10 m/s. At what angle with the vertical must he hold his umbrella to protect himself?
questions.explanation: Relative velocity of rain has horizontal component 10 m/s and vertical component 10 m/s. Angle with vertical is tan(θ) = 10 / 10 = 1 -> θ = 45 degrees.

questions.q: A particle is projected at an angle θ with the horizontal. At what time t is the velocity vector perpendicular to the initial velocity vector?
questions.explanation: For the velocity vector to be perpendicular to the initial velocity, their dot product must be zero, yielding t = u / (g sin(θ)).

questions.q: A body starts from rest and moves with uniform acceleration. The ratio of distances covered in the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd seconds is:
questions.explanation: Distance in the n-th second is proportional to (2n-1). For n=1, 2, 3: (2(1)-1) : (2(2)-1) : (2(3)-1) = 1 : 3 : 5.

questions.q: Two particles are projected simultaneously from the same point with the same speed u at angles of elevation θ1 and θ2 complementary to each other. If they reach the same maximum height, what is the ratio of their maximum heights H1 / H2?
questions.explanation: If θ2 = 90° - θ1, then H1 / H2 = sin²(θ1) / sin²(90°-θ1) = sin²(θ1) / cos²(θ1) = tan²(θ1).

questions.q: A stone is thrown upwards from a tower of height 50 m with a velocity of 20 m/s. What is its striking velocity when it hits the ground? (g = 10 m/s²)
A projectile is launched with velocity u at an angle θ. Its velocity at any general time t during flight is given by:
questions.explanation: Horizontal velocity is vx = u cos(θ) and vertical velocity is vy = u sin(θ) - gt. Magnitude of resultant velocity is sqrt(vx² + vy²).
